description: Heritage `value of … for key` given a KEY that is neither word nor number raises the byte-identical Core `ol-type` the `:ages[:k]` selector raises — `expected: "word or number"`, `operation: "index"`, message "index needs a word or number, but got a list." This is the reader's third failure mode, and the one the container-type fixtures cannot reach: it turns on the KEY, not the operand, so its Core twin is the RUNTIME-key selector `:ages[:k]` rather than the dotted `:ages.tom` the container-type fixtures twin (a dotted key is a parse-time identifier, so it has no runtime-key failure mode to be a twin of). The key is bound to `:k` on both sides so the two spellings supply the SAME evaluated value: an inline `:ages[[ 1 2 ]]` does not parse, and `:ages[true]` means the literal word "true" (`spec/grammar.md:260`) while `for key true` evaluates a boolean. Added with issue #784 to close the last condition of this reader that had unit coverage but no stack-neutral proof. NO Heritage spelling in any payload (issue #670). The span points at the reader's `:k` key sub-expression (localization-only difference — `spec/localization.md`). Heritage depends on Data (`spec/conformance.md:305`), so both `data` and `heritage` are active.

diagnostics.message: index needs a word or number, but got a list.
